title: Householder Mirror task Views
hypothesis: For task Views generated by short Householder products, one shared D×D operator plus per-task reflection vectors reproduces independent full operators exactly with lower serialized bytes; matrix-free reflection compute grows with reflection count and must be compared with dense OFT and parameter-matched block-orthogonal controls.
physical_object: one shared FP32 D×D linear operator W
mirror_coordinate: per-task product of r Householder reflection vectors
logical_multiplicity: 16 linear task functions over one shared operator
controls: shared W plus dense per-task OFT orthogonal matrices
native Householder parameterization with exact same function and bytes

development.selection_metric: function output NRMSE, actual serialized bytes, and matrix-vector FLOP proxy

paid_objects: dense OFT matrices for OFT control
block orthogonal matrices for parameter-matched control

success_gate: Across all audit seeds, Householder output NRMSE <=1e-5 versus independent operators and complete payload <=50% independent at r<=4; report FLOP overhead versus independent and compare same-budget block-orthogonal quality. Native exact alias means no Mirror-specific value.
failure_gate: Any audit seed exceeds 1e-5 function error or r<=4 payload exceeds 50% independent; exact native Householder alias is FAIL for Mirror-specific attribution regardless of feasibility.
boundaries: Synthetic linear operator functions only; no trained PEFT model, downstream task quality, or GPU throughput claim.
Task functions are generated from the candidate reflection family by construction; no learning/capacity claim.
Block control is an oracle projection onto block-orthogonal matrices and is a parameter-matched geometry control, not a trained BOFT/GSOFT result.
